payload.purpose_context: The Quadrano talk on Thu 19 Nov needs a real website whose data layer Quadrano can validate on stage. This mission builds a small static shop with its own GTM container, buttons that push correct and deliberately broken add_to_cart and purchase events, and a scenario switcher that walks the demo script, so the audience sees Quadrano's Console verdicts on genuine pushes. It must be demoable by Sun 8 Nov and run clean in three rehearsals by Thu 19 Nov.
payload.purpose_tldr: A static mini-shop at demo.quadrano.com whose correct and deliberately broken data layer pushes let the Quadrano talk show live validation.

options: Quadrano runtime only, Console format v1 verbatim
Shop also shows its own expected-result hint
payload.question: Who produces the pass/fail verdicts and messages the audience sees: the Quadrano runtime (via the GTM snippet) in Console format v1 verbatim, or the shop itself?

payload.final_answer: Quadrano runtime only, Console format v1 verbatim. The shop logs nothing verdict-like; acceptance is measured against the v1 lines; transaction_id is required so the transaction_ID scenario fails.

options: Plan: 5 broken scenarios incl. bad regex, 5 pages
payload.question: Which broken scenarios and pages are in scope: the brief's four broken pushes on a minimal shop, or the build plan's five (adding a bad transaction_id regex) across listing, product, basket, checkout and thank-you pages?

payload.final_answer: Five broken scenarios including bad transaction_id regex (as a spare beyond the talk script); the five plan pages (listing, product, basket, checkout, thank-you) kept deliberately thin; switcher can jump to any page+scenario.

payload.question: What shape do add_to_cart and purchase pushes take: flat top-level Attributes (value, currency, transaction_id beside event) or GA4 ecommerce-nested (ecommerce.value, ecommerce.items[])? And which Attributes does add_to_cart carry?

payload.final_answer: GA4 ecommerce-nested. add_to_cart: ecommerce.currency, ecommerce.value, ecommerce.items[] (item_id, item_name, price, quantity); purchase adds ecommerce.transaction_id. Each ecommerce push preceded by {ecommerce: null}. Exact Attribute names provisional until W2 freeze Tue 27 Oct.

payload.question: How should the GTM container ID reach the served pages: baked in at build time from a Cloudflare Pages build environment variable, or injected per request by a Cloudflare Pages Function?
How should production deploys run: Cloudflare Pages Git integration building from main (GitHub Actions runs the gates on PRs), or GitHub Actions running the gates then deploying with wrangler?

Does C-009 (pnpm, Vite, TypeScript, ESLint) cover the supporting dev dependencies typescript-eslint and @eslint/js, with gate scripts written in TypeScript run by Node 24 LTS native type stripping (no tsx, husky or gitleaks)?

payload.final_answer: Build-time Cloudflare Pages env var (VITE_GTM_CONTAINER_ID) baked into built HTML by Vite; never in repo; missing ID builds pages without GTM.
Cloudflare Pages Git integration builds and deploys main; GitHub Actions runs pnpm gates on every push and PR; main changes only via PR with green gates.
Yes, covered by C-009: typescript-eslint and @eslint/js allowed; gate scripts in TypeScript run by Node 24 LTS native type stripping; no tsx, husky or gitleaks; pre-push hook via core.hooksPath.

options: No, keep five packages and exclude scripts from type checking
payload.question: Is @types/node (type-only, no runtime code) covered by C-009 so that gate scripts and vite.config.ts get full tsc and type-aware lint checking?

payload.final_answer: Yes, covered by C-009: @types/node allowed as a type-only dev dependency, pinned, recorded in AGENTS.md; scripts/ and vite.config.ts are fully type-checked and type-aware linted.
payload.rationale: Type definitions only; no runtime code and nothing shipped to the browser. Confirmed by the Product Owner at /spec-kitty.tasks.
